answer: At the nadir of Byzantine fault tolerance the protocol fixes a deterministic quorum Q = ceil(2n/3) so any two quorums intersect in > n/3 honest nodes, making malicious quorum intersection impossible for f < n/3. Staking collateral C, slashing penalty S, and a zero-knowledge verifiable delay VDF yield negative expected attack utility and a robust Nash equilibrium for state-machine replication, while the falcon validator set emits a signal committing each checkpoint.
